thread.title: Nick's Picks Halftime Report: Beating The Market Once Again

author: Nicholas Ward
title: Nick's Picks Halftime Report: Beating The Market Once Again
text:
It’s the 4 th of July, the heat has died down, the grill has been cleaned, and the fireworks are over with. I’ve decided to spend the rest of my evening putting together a halftime report for my annual Nick’s Picks portfolio. It’s worth noting that it’s not quite halftime (technically, I should have done this piece last weekend). All year-to-date figures in this piece were totaled up today. With that said, I am still incredibly pleased with my results thus far.
Every year, my stated goal with this portfolio is to beat the market. For those of you who aren’t familiar with Nick’s Picks, here’s a little recap. I began this theoretical portfolio project in 2016. Let me repeat, this is a theoretical portfolio. While I do own many of these names in my actual portfolio, Nick’s Picks is a project focused around compounding fake money.
I take a few more risks with Nick’s Picks than I do in my actual portfolio. The weightings in this portfolio are more concentrated. The focus isn’t so much on dividends and dividend growth, but instead, on total returns. With that said, since I spend the vast majority of my time doing due diligence on DGI names, the majority of the holdings in the Nick’s Picks portfolio are indeed dividend growers.
In January of 2016 , I gave myself $100,000.00 to “invest” in an attempt to beat the market in both the short and long terms. I build the portfolio every year in January, let it sit until December 31, add in the dividends received throughout the year, and then start the process again.
During 2016, the portfolio grew from $100,000.00 to $116,499.16. During 2017, Nick’s Picks grew from $116,499.16 to $143,174.65. So, on January 1 this year , I put together a portfolio using that $143,174.65, and here’s what I came up with:

What’s more, my growth figure doesn’t include the dividends I’ve “received” in the first half. Since I don’t reinvest dividends until the following year in the Nick’s Picks project, I decided to save the time tallying them up until December. The Nick’s Picks portfolio yield isn’t as high as that of my actual portfolios, but in 2017 it generated nearly $2,500.00 worth of dividends, and I expect that figure to be even higher in 2018.
First-Half Breakdown There have definitely been some surprises thus far throughout the first half of the year. I had no idea that we’d experience this sort of volatility in the markets, that’s for sure. There are some high-beta names in Nick’s Picks this year, and thankfully, they’ve held up well. As a matter of fact, my growth names are what have carried me along to market-beating gains.
Thankfully, I own most of these high-growth names in my actual portfolio as well. Looking at the portfolio, Amazon’s performance is certainly worth noting. It’s been absolutely fantastic throughout 2018. I trimmed a bit of my AMZN earlier in the year in my actual portfolio, locking in large gains, but even so, the remaining shares make up a large position and I’m happy to have let those run.
I have exposure to all of the Chinese internet names included in Nick’s Picks as well. These stocks have gotten caught up in the trade war rhetoric in recent weeks, and this has hurt their YTD returns; however, I wholeheartedly expect to see a solid second half from them.
Why? Well, first of all because their sales/earnings are growing like weeds. I know many investors question the validity of these numbers due to suspicions of faulty Chinese accounting practices and the lack of transparency, though I feel comfortable owning shares of the big internet names like Alibaba, Tencent, and JD.com in both Nick’s Picks and my personal portfolio as speculative growth names.
And second, I think the market will eventually realize that these names aren’t dependent on the U.S. market for growth. I think any tariffs/trade spats will have minimal effects on the top line growth for a name like BABA. The Chinese market alone is more than big enough for this company to post strong double-digit growth for years. I’m also sure that these Chinese big-tech names will continue to make inroads in international markets in southeast Asia and across the world.
The only growth name that I only “own” in Nick’s Picks is Salesforce.com. CRM has been a part of the Nick’s Picks project since 2017. I “bought” my 40-share position in January of 2017 for $2738.40, and thus far, it’s more than doubled to $5513.60.
In hindsight, I wish that I had actually bought shares of CRM for $68, but the fundamental valuations have always been hard to justify here. I must tip my hat to Marc Benioff and thank him for contributing to my success here with Nick’s Picks.
One of the major surprises for me regarding this portfolio thus far in 2018 is the underperformance of the financials. Blackstone is doing well, but everyone else, from Berkshire to the big banks, has posted negative returns on the year. I assumed that rising rates would have been a steady wind at the back of these names. I didn’t foresee the yield curve narrowing so quickly though, and this has certainly put a damper on the de-regulatory environment that they’re now operating in.
Thankfully, CCAR results just came in, and we saw strong capital return allocations from the banks. The financials have benefitted from seasonal tailwinds in the second half of 2016 and 2017, so hopefully that trend continues in 2018 so that these stocks can help add to Nick’s Picks gains before the year is over.
I also didn’t foresee the destruction on value that we’ve seen in the telecom/media space thus far this year. Disney is a core holding in Nick’s Picks as well as in my actual portfolio. DIS shares have been lagging for a couple of years now, and I keep waiting for the market to come to its senses so that these undervalued shares can break out. Maybe that will happen in the second half if the bidding war for Fox (NASDAQ: FOX ) comes to an end.
Speaking of the bidding war for Fox, I can’t believe how badly Comcast has performed. This is one of my favorite dividend growth names. CMCSA hasn’t disappointed in that regard with its most recent 20.6% dividend increase announcement in January. However, the shares are down double digits, and in a 1-year portfolio like Nick’s Picks, this really hurts.
AT&T is down big too. I’m very bullish on all of these content/media related names, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see them bounce back in the second half. Only time will tell though, and I wouldn’t hold your breath if I was you, because I’ve obviously been on the wrong side of this trade for some time now (as you can see, Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX ) was not one of Nick’s Picks in 2017 or 2018 after it posted strong performance for this project portfolio in 2016).
Conclusion I actually really like the situation I’m in here with Nick’s Picks heading into the second half of the year. I think I’m sitting on a handful of beaten-down, coiled springs here. I think that all three of my core positions - Apple, Johnson and Johnson, and Disney - could post double-digit gains between now and the end of the year. I think the financials as well as the media names could bounce back as well. I expect recent stalwarts like Boeing and Nvidia to continue their strong performance, backed by strong fundamental growth. I think the Chinese names could still be portfolio leaders, even though the first half of 2018 has been subpar for them. And lastly, I think adding in the dividend income produced by this portfolio will help to widen the gap between me and the S&P 500.
So, there’s your update. We’ll revisit this portfolio at the end of December. Until then, I hope all are well!
Disclosure: I am/we are long AAPL, DIS, JNJ, AMZN, GOOGL, BABA, TCEHY, JD, BA, UTX, AMGN, MRK, PFE, HON, CSCO, NVDA, BAC, BRK.B, JPM, BUD, CMCSA, VZ, T, NKE.
